Sita Ram International LLP, is a partnership firm and engaged in the business of import & trading of Timber at its registered office as mentioned in memo of parties. It is claimed that defendant no.1, which is an Overseas Private Ltd. company, is running its business through its Managing Director (defendant no. 2) and dealing in Imported Timber woods and other allied products. It is further the case of the plaintiff that defendants came into its contact through the Managing Director of A.S. Wood Impex Pvt. Ltd., as plaintiff was interested to purchase the M/S Sita Ram International Llp vs Gauri Trading Pte Ltd. However, the defendants only sent a proforma invoice bearing no. PI-024/2018 bearing dated 12/06/2018 on the official whatsapp number of the plaintiff's firm at Delhi, with a condition for advance payment of 25% of the total estimated value of USD 1,20,000/- as per said invoice and accordingly, plaintiff paid the said advance amount of USD 30,000/- through its banker Karur Vysya Bank, Branch at Ramesh Nagar, Delhi, to the account of defendants through Outward TT FCY on 13-06-2018 but despite getting the advance CS (COMM.) Page No.2 of 17 payment, defendants failed to perform their promise as the actual final packing list as per shape and size of the said goods was not provided to the plaintiff despite specific request for the same. 2. It is further claimed by the plaintiff that meanwhile defendant no.2 made a request to the plaintiff to purchase the sample consignment of same quality of Cedar Wood, having quantity of 149.084 CBM, at the price of USD 240 CBM, which was actually shipped for another supplier Veer Timber at Gandhi Dham, but that buyer had refused to take the said consignment. Considering the problem of the defendants, the plaintiff agreed for the same and accordingly defendants had issued a sales contract bearing no. 030/2018 dated 17/07/2018 qua the same along with actual packing list, which the plaintiff got released after getting the NOC provided from the previous buyer and by making the entire payment of USD 35,780.16 to the defendants on 23-07-2018 through bank transfer via outward TT FCY. It is further averred that despite the fact that the plaintiff had got released to the defendants above said consignment, the defendants did not provide the actual packing/log list as required by the Plaintiff in reply to their previous invoice no. PI 024/18 dated 12-06-2018 even after repeated telephonic requests till the date of shipment i.e. 31-07-2018 and also till 21-08-2018, which was the last date of negotiation as per the said invoice. Therefore on 22-08-2018, the plaintiff made a specific request to defendant no.2 telephonically to refund the aforesaid advance sum of USD 30,000 received by the defendants on 13-06-2018 against invoice dated 12/06/2018, which the defendants assured to repay to the plaintiff within a period of 2 week. But on 03-09-2018, the defendants again sent a sales contract no. 040/2018 of the Cedar SPP with an offer to sell at the lowest price of USD 216 per CBM for the quantity of 500 CBM but the plaintiff was not interested to purchase the same and accordingly did not accept the said offer by not signing the agreement/contract and rather reminded the defendants to refund the advance sum of the plaintiff. It is further claimed that despite the specific denial and refusal to accept defendants offer at the lowest price in respect of the said consignment, defendants adopted an unfair trade practice by creating unnecessary pressure upon the plaintiff to get release the cargo and therefore, on 22-09- 2018, an e-mail was sent by the defendants with an intimation that defendants are going to sell the consignment in open market to CS (COMM.) It is further claimed by the plaintiff that on 20-10-2018, the defendants again sent an e-mail to the plaintiff's representative stating that the defendants were going to sell the Cargo @ USD 160 to some other buyer at risk and cost of the plaintiff, which mail was also duly responded by the plaintiff on the same day at about 9:21 p.m. (IST) with a repeated request and reminder to refund the aforesaid advance amount of USD 30,000/- (equivalent to Indian currency of Rs. 20,33,400/-) along with interest @ 18 % p.a. w.e.f. 13-06-2018 till payment is made to the plaintiff. It is further claimed by the plaintiff that the defendants were also apprised that the goods/material worth USD 35,780.16 purchased vide invoice dated 12-07-2018, was with deficient/incomplete documents, the PHYTO Sanitary certificate was also not according to safety standards/concern prevailing as per Indian CS (COMM.) texts.arguments: 3. It is further the case of the plaintiff that since the defendants did CS (COMM.) No.868/2022 M/s. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.3 of 17 not fulfill their promise by not meeting out the necessary requirements and demand of the plaintiff within the agreed period as per the said invoice, therefore, the said transaction failed due to the defendants negligent conduct, which also reflects that defendants did not have the stock of the said goods offered for sale to the plaintiff vide the said invoice even till the last date of negotiation i.e. 21-08-2018. 9. In support of its case, plaintiff has examined two witnesses, namely, PW-1 Sarthak Singhal, partner of the plaintiff and PW-Sh Amit Kumar, Assistant Manager, Officer Scale-I, Karur Vysya M/S Sita Ram International Llp vs Gauri Trading Pte Ltd. On the said aspect, Ld Counsel for the defendants has stated that the suit against the defendant no. 2 Director is not maintainable in the absence of his tortious liability qua any fraud proved by the plaintiff or in the absence of any personal guarantee of said Director. 15. Per contra, Ld Counsel for the plaintiff has claimed that defendant no. 2 being Director of defendant no. 1 company, is fully liable qua the outstanding amount due against the company. To substantiate his claim that defendant no. 2 has been rightly made a party to the suit, Ld Counsel for the plaintiff has relied upon following judgments: (1) Subhra Mukherjee & Anr. Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. & Ors (2000) 3 SCC 312 CS (COMM.) No.868/2022 M/s. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.9 of 17 (2) Singer India Ltd. v. Chander Mohan Chadha & Ors., V (2004) SLT 102-(2004) 7 SCC 1 (3) Saurabh Exports Vs. Blaze Finlease & Credits Pvt. Ltd. 129 (2006) DLT 429 16. As regards the liability of the directors of a company in a civil suit, reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of 'Mukesh Hans and Ors. V. Uma Bhasin & Ors.", RFA 14/2010 and CM No. 495/2010, date of decision:-16.08.2010, MANU/DE/2160/2010 as well as in the case of 'Sanju Batla & Anr. Vs. Manu Maheshwari & Anr.', C.R.P. No. 166/2018, decided on 12.04.2021, relevant part of which is reproduced below:- "28. Learned counsel for the Petitioner has rightly relied on the judgment of the Co-ordinate Bench in Mukesh Hans (supra), which, in my view, squarely covers the M/S Sita Ram International Llp vs Gauri Trading Pte Ltd. Relevant passages from the judgment are as follows :- "10. The decisions of the Company are taken by the Board of Directors of a Company. International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.10 of 17 Company by acting on its behalf, unless he is so authorized to act by a special resolution passed by the Board or unless the Articles of Association so warrant. It is equally well settled that a Director of a Company though he owes a fiduciary duty to the Company, he owes no contractual duty qua third parties. The first is where the Director or Directors make themselves personally liable, i.e., by execution of personal guarantees, indemnities, etc. The second is where a Director induces a third party to act to his detriment by advancing a loan or money to the Company. On the third party proving such fraudulent misrepresentation, a Director may be held personally liable to the said third party. Also, Ld Counsel for the plaintiff did not dispute that in the plaint there is no assertion against defendant no. 2 that he personally undertook or agreed to clear any liability of the defendant no. 1 outstanding against the plaintiff. Accordingly, in view of the CS (COMM.) No.868/2022 M/s. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.11 of 17 aforesaid judgment relied upon by this court and in the facts and circumstances of this case, defendant no. 2 Ganesh Arora Managing Director of defendant no. 1 company, is neither necessary nor a proper party merely on the ground that he had acted as Managing Director on behalf of defendant no.1 company, while transactions between the plaintiff and the defendant no. 1 company were carried out. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.12 of 17 dated 12-07-2018 Ex. PW-1/7(Colly.) qua goods supplied to the plaintiff by the defendant worth USD 35,780. However, the plaintiff has sought damages to the tune of Rs. 2,85,134/- since the aforesaid order was received with deficient/incomplete documents viz. PHYTO Sanitary certificate being not in accordance to safety standards/concern prevailing as per Indian Law and the transfer of ownership of the said consignment in name of the plaintiff from the previous owner/supplier was not done within the prescribed period as per Indian Law. 19. Since Ld Counsel for the defendants had strongly raised the dispute with regard to the existence of the territorial jurisdiction of this court to deal with the present matter and the same goes to the root of the matter, therefore the same has to be decided first. 20. On the said aspect, during the course of arguments, Ld Counsel for the plaintiff has relied upon on the principle that "Debtor must seek the creditor" and has cited the following judgments in support of his contention that this court has the territorial jurisdiction to try and entertain the present suit: (1)Mrs. Shradha Wassan & Ors. Vs. Anil Goyal & Anr. (CS no. 2045/2007) (2) Arcelormittal India Pvt. Ltd. Vs. JSC Ogcc Kazstroyservice in CS (Comm) no. 592/22 dated 30.05.2023 (3) A.B.C. Laminart Pvt. Ltd. Vs. A.P. Agencies 21 . However, in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the CS (COMM.) No.868/2022 M/s. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.13 of 17 cased titled as M/s. Auto Movers Vs Luminous Power Technologies Pvt Ltd. in CM (M) No. 604/2020, Cm Appeal No. 30745/2020 decided on 16-09-2021, wherein in para 19, it is held as under: "19.The Trial Court has followed the decision of this court in Satyapal (supra) that where the place of payment has not been fixed, as appears to be the case here, payment was to be made at the place of the creditor i.e., at Delhi in the present case. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner/defendant that Satyapal (supra) was decided in the manner it did, only because the contract was entered into at Delhi M/S Sita Ram International Llp vs Gauri Trading Pte Ltd. And Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125466024/ 7 and the orders were placed at Delhi, is not wholly correct, inasmuch as this court had quoted with approval, the judgment of the learned Trial Court, which clearly held that in cases where the place of payment was not specified in the contracts/bills/invoices, parties had to follow the general rule that the payment had to be made at the place of the creditor." 22. Page No.14 of 17 the seller as Indian Bank Singapore Branch, 3 Raffles Place, Bharat Building, Singapore 048617 Swift Code IDIB SGSG, Account No. 302334008 and payment terms mention payment through banking mode. 23. On territorial jurisdiction, reliance may be placed upon the landmark order of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Dentsply India Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Excel International & Ors., CS (OS) No. 410/1999, date of decision:-10.07.2012, wherein it was held in para no. 5 as under:- 5. In a contractual matter, the jurisdiction of a Court arises from four aspects. The first is where the contract is entered into. Second is where the contract is to be performed. The third is where moneys have to be paid under the contract and fourthly where the defendants in the suit are residing or voluntary working for gain. This is the ratio of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of ABC Laminart Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. vs. A.P.Agencies, Salem, AIR 1989 SC 1239. If there is more than one Court which has territorial jurisdiction, then parties by contract can restrict the jurisdiction to one or more of the Courts which have jurisdiction, however, parties by consent cannot confer jurisdiction on a Court which otherwise does not have any. In the present case the only reason which is urged for pleading CS (COMM.) No.868/2022 M/s. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.15 of 17 that this Court has no territorial jurisdiction is because the goods are alleged to be supplied by the plaintiff from its godowns at Gurgaon, taken with the fact that all the invoices specifically contain the condition that only the Courts in Haryana will have exclusive territorial jurisdiction. 24. On the territorial jurisdiction aspect, even if for arguments sake it is assumed that the plaintiff had placed orders upon the defendant from its office situated in Pitam Pura, Delhi, made an advance payment of 30,000 USD to the defendants at Singapore through its Banker Karur Vysya M/S Sita Ram International Llp vs Gauri Trading Pte Ltd. And Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125466024/ 8 Bank, Ramesh Nagar Branch, Delhi, still from the same on the basis of Dentsply India Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Excel International & Ors.(supra), it cannot be inferred that any of the aforesaid four conditions required for making out territorial jurisdiction of this court to deal with the matter are satisfied or it can be assumed that the territorial jurisdiction to deal with the matter would be with the court within whose jurisdiction office of the plaintiff at Pitam Pura, Delhi, is situated. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.16 of 17 was to be performed within the territorial jurisdiction of this court.

On the territorial jurisdiction aspect, even if for arguments sake it is assumed that the plaintiff had placed orders upon the defendant from its office situated in Pitam Pura, Delhi, made an advance payment of 30,000 USD to the defendants at Singapore through its Banker Karur Vysya M/S Sita Ram International Llp vs Gauri Trading Pte Ltd. And Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125466024/ 8 Bank, Ramesh Nagar Branch, Delhi, still from the same on the basis of Dentsply India Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Excel International & Ors.(supra), it cannot be inferred that any of the aforesaid four conditions required for making out territorial jurisdiction of this court to deal with the matter are satisfied or it can be assumed that the territorial jurisdiction to deal with the matter would be with the court within whose jurisdiction office of the plaintiff at Pitam Pura, Delhi, is situated. Sita Ram International LLP Vs Gauri Trading PTE Ltd. & Anr. Page No.16 of 17 was to be performed within the territorial jurisdiction of this court.
